fullDesc: Key Features: Dimensions : 33mm x 21mm Hx711 Chip : The core of the module is the Hx711 chip, a 24-bit precision analog-to-digital converter (ADC) designed specifically for load cell applications. Load Cell Interface : The module connects to strain gauge load cells, which convert physical pressure into electrical signals. It measures very small voltage changes from the load cell. High Precision : The Hx711 offers a high-resolution reading with a precision of up to 24 bits, ensuring accurate weight measurement. Low Power Consumption : Ideal for battery-operated devices. Selectable Gain : The module allows selectable gains of 32, 64, or 128 to adapt to different load cell outputs. Analog Input : It amplifies low-amplitude analog signals from the load cell and converts them into digital form for microcontroller interfaces like Arduino or Raspberry Pi. Simple Wiring : It uses only 2 data lines (clock and data) to communicate with the microcontroller, simplifying the design. Applications : Commonly used in digital weighing scales, industrial process control, and precision force sensors. Pin Description: VCC : Power supply (typically 2.6V to 5.5V) GND : Ground DT (Data) : Data output from the Hx711 to the microcontroller SCK (Clock) : Clock signal for synchronous data transfer This sensor module is widely used in electronic scales and pressure measurement systems due to its high accuracy and ease of use. fullDesc: A Plug Power Cord Adapter Cable is a flexible electrical cable that connects a device to a power adapter or directly to an electrical outlet. Here are its main features: Plug End (Power Source Connector) : This end connects to the power source, usually a wall socket. The plug design depends on the country or region, with different prong configurations (e.g., Type A for the U.S., Type C for Europe, etc.). Cable (Insulated Wire) : The main body of the adapter is the cable itself, which contains insulated wires to safely transfer electricity from the power source to the connected device. The length of the cable can vary, and it’s typically covered with durable insulation, often made of rubber or PVC, to prevent electrical hazards. Adapter Unit (if applicable) : Some cords include an inline adapter or transformer that modifies the voltage or converts alternating current (AC) to direct current (DC), ensuring that the connected device receives the appropriate power. Device Connector : The end of the cable that plugs into the device varies in shape and size, depending on the device’s power port. Common connectors include barrel jacks (for laptops), USB connectors (for phones), or proprietary connectors (for specific appliances). Safety Features : Some power cord adapters include fuses, surge protectors, or thermal cutoffs to protect the connected device from electrical surges or overheating. Use Case : These cables are widely used for powering electronic devices such as laptops, desktops, monitors, home appliances, and other gadgets. They ensure that devices can be powered safely and effectively by adapting to different power outlets or providing the necessary voltage conversion. fullDesc: The 74×266 (ex 74HC266) is a chip with four open-collector XNOR gates. Open-collector outputs make it simple to connect to other chips that use different logic levels. But it also means you can’t use this chip as a direct replacement for a normal XNOR gate chip. In this guide, you will learn all about this chip and how you can use its XNOR gates in your own circuit. What does the 74HC266 / 74LS266 do? The 74×266 gives you four open-collector XNOR gates that can be used individually. An XNOR gate is a logic gate that outputs 1 (HIGH) if its inputs are equal (both 1 or both 0). In the truth table below, you can see what the output will be for any given input: Truth table for the XNOR gate How To Use This Chip The 74HC266 comes in a 14-pin package, and you need to connect it to power before you can use it. Most 7400 ICs support a VCC voltage of 5V. One difference between the HC and LS version of the chip is that the 74HC266 supports 2V to 6V, while the 74LS266 only supports 5V. Once it’s connected, you can use any of the four open-collector XNOR gates inside. The 74HC266/74LS266 IC connected to power This chip uses open-collector outputs . That means you can only sink current (current can flow into the chip), not source it (current cannot flow out of the chip). Each gate output of the 74HC266 can sink about 4 mA when powered with 5V. While the 74LS266 can usually sink about 8 mA of current. These values can vary between manufacturers of the chip though. How To Use Open-Collector Outputs The outputs from the 74HC266 are not your normal high/low outputs. Instead, they use something called open-collector .
